correctness.rationale: The defined full strong-Morse complex uses all 720 orders of the one-dimensional triangular-prism graph and matching incidences with exactly one earlier neighbor. Independently reconstructed 18 directed incidence vertices and nonempty face vector (18,66,24), then greedy incidence-toggle matching gives 41 cover pairs and 26 critical faces (one vertex, 25 edges). Independently built all 204 Hasse covers, reversed matching arrows and topologically sorted all 108 nonempty faces, verifying acyclicity; Forman theory yields integral wedge^25 S1 and π1 free rank25. Independently enumerated all 12 S3×C2 automorphisms and signed simplex traces: identity 25, layer swap and 3cycles 1, transpositions −1. This is χ=2regular+inflated sign, invariants=2. The exact domain is the full strong matching construction for one unfilled prism, not ordinary/pure complexes.
residual_risks: Independent source paper on strong-Morse definition body unavailable; the package explicitly defines the evaluated complex. Integral group-module decomposition not asserted.

originality.rationale: The full strong Morse complex is materially different from the ordinary Morse complex of the same six-vertex prism. The published ordinary complex is a 64-fold wedge S^4 on 1,727 faces; this explicit strong subcomplex has 108 faces and a 25-circle wedge, plus a twelve-element symmetry module character. The Knudson-Owens-White primary introduction names other graph families in its accessible abstract. Best-of-knowledge not universal-priority.
residual_risks: Full Knudson-Owens-White primary manuscript was inaccessible; any prism example in its body or appendix remains unverified.

The identification of total-order-generated matchings with the full Knudson strong-Morse construction rests on the displayed definition in the audited package; no independent body-text verification was possible.

value.rationale: The triangular prism is the smallest multi-cycle cubic prism outside the path, cycle and star examples. The exact strong-Morse homotopy type and full symmetry character distinguish it sharply from the previously known ordinary Morse complex on the same graph, providing a concrete integral/topological benchmark for strong matching complexes.
residual_risks: Judgment addresses mathematical motivation of the exact invariant, not expected citations or paper-sized impact.

limitations: Unfilled one-dimensional triangular prism only; full strong-Morse complex, not ordinary or pure complex; integral homotopy but only rational symmetry splitting.
